batteryPack.title: Battery Pack Fault Procedure
steps: Check that battery voltage and state of charge are within normal limits.
Measure internal resistance and capacity, then compare them with baseline values.
If voltage is abnormal and internal resistance is increasing, investigate battery aging or a short circuit.
If temperature is elevated, inspect the thermal management system.
Determine whether immediate landing or maintenance is required based on severity.

powerElectronics.title: Power Electronics Fault Procedure
steps: Monitor input and output voltage and current waveforms.
Inspect switching component temperatures and cooling performance.
Verify that drive signals are operating normally.
Abnormal voltage with resistance drift may indicate an inverter or DC/DC converter fault.
Shut down and inspect if unusual noise or significant vibration is present.

airframe.title: Airframe Structural Fault Procedure
steps: Visually inspect the airframe for cracks, deformation, or loose fasteners.
Measure the vibration spectrum and look for resonant frequencies.
Check torque at primary structural joints.
A sudden vibration increase with normal RPM may indicate rotor imbalance or structural fatigue.
Perform ultrasonic or radiographic inspection when required.

avionics.title: Avionics Fault Procedure
steps: Check that cockpit instrument displays are operating normally.
Check communication links for interruptions or error codes.
Test navigation, attitude, and flight control signals.
Simultaneous sensor anomalies may indicate electromagnetic interference or a grounding issue.
Run the avionics built-in test (BIT) if needed.

coolingSystem.title: Cooling System Fault Procedure
steps: Check coolant flow and temperature distribution.
Measure radiator airflow or coolant pump pressure.
Inspect cooling passages for blockages or leaks.
Concurrent temperature and voltage drift may indicate reduced cooling performance.
Clean the radiator or replace a faulty fan.

bearing.title: Bearing Wear Procedure
steps: Monitor bearing temperature and vibration spectrum.
Inspect lubricant condition and contamination levels.
Concurrent increases in bearing temperature and vibration may indicate insufficient lubrication or fatigue.
Estimate remaining useful life from vibration trends.
Plan bearing replacement when alert thresholds are reached.

batteryThermalManagement.title: Battery Thermal Management Fault Procedure
steps: Check whether battery pack surface temperatures are uniform.
Measure coolant flow and pressure.
A rapid state-of-charge drop with high temperature may indicate thermal runaway risk.
Initiate emergency cooling or isolation procedures.
Follow fire response procedures if smoke or unusual odors are present.
